The withdrawal base this row waited on has landed, and what remains is narrower than the row previously said. src/composition/facet-withdrawal.ts#FacetWithdrawal retires every Workspace-owned record of one exact contribution in one caller transaction, recomputing the exact FacetRef and PackagePin set inside it, so a Facet can now be withdrawn mid-Turn. The one mechanism this rule's typed-unavailability clause still needs is W2's, not W3's. A withdrawn captured member must yield a typed unavailability at its NEXT use, which requires a retired-Binding state for a resolution attempt to observe; C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT records that authority-owned Bindings and Grants still need their own owning-Actor transaction and Scope epoch advance in src/authority, and no cross-Actor transaction will be added. The behaviour test the rule requires stays unwritten for that reason, and no partial selector is cited in its place. It must prove both halves in one exercise and fail if either is traded for the other: an install and a withdrawal committed mid-Turn leave the Turn's membership identical, while a Grant revoked mid-Turn denies the next use of a member the Turn still composes. A test asserting only stable membership would pass against a host that had frozen authority with it.

remainingEvidence: Publication is now the commit point in the durable sense as well as the logical one, and the two commit points §5.6 describes are two construction paths rather than one. TurnAdmissionVerifier.admit builds an Invocation-identity handle over an AdmittedInvocationItem — invocation, item index, item key and the exact EffectAttempt — and reads no Receipt at all, which is what a detached admission leaves behind. A child RunRef handle keeps the Receipt-based path, because a child reference exists only once the delegate Receipt carries it; the spawn Receipt and its result digest moved onto that identity case, so an Invocation identity has no field they could occupy.

TurnAdmissionPublisher.publish reserves the Run obligation and appends the Invocation owner's admission message in one Run transaction, and RunRuntime.terminalizeRunInTransaction appends one cancellation message per still-owed published item in the same transition that terminalizes the Run. A response lost after that transaction commits loses no command: RunRuntime.pendingInvocationDeliveries replays each message after a restart, and RunRuntime.acknowledgeInvocationDelivery discharges it idempotently with no caller-supplied revision, because an owner whose acknowledgement response was lost knows no current revision.

The Run ships no §7.4 verdict, and has no field for one. TurnAdmissionHandle.cancelledBy and RunTerminalization.cancelled are deleted rather than deprecated: the Run observed its own end, not whether cancellation reached a live target controller, and after a restart there is no controller left to reach. What the Run owes is a request naming the exact attempt; the Invocation owner's target aborts the controller keyed by that attempt and the existing AttemptFailureKind.classify path derives `aborted` from what the target observed, while an absent controller leaves the outcome indeterminate for reconciliation.

The prohibition on the issuing Turn's cancellation reaching a published item holds by identity: TextId compares its constructor, so a published item's owner, always a RunId, never equals a cancelled TurnId. An item no Turn published is reached by neither scope, which is C13-FACET-CANCELLATION-REACH's rule and not this one's.

Which handles a Run cancellation can address is decided by the item's Receipt state, not by the method that built the handle, and the distinction matters for anyone reading this row. cancellationDeliveriesInTransaction skips an item whose current Receipt is terminal before it resolves the handle at all. TurnAdmissionVerifier.verify returns only on the succeeded evidence shape, and a succeeded AttemptReceipt is terminal, so a verify-built handle is never addressed in a truthful state; §7.4 admits supersession only of `indeterminate`, which that path never accepts, so the gate cannot open. An admit-built handle names an attempt no Receipt names yet, so it is addressed until its own Receipt lands.

That argument rests on one host-supplied premise, stated here rather than hidden: invocationItemTerminal is a predicate on the abstract SettlementEvidencePort, and the runtime trusts it. A host that answered it untruthfully would address an item that already has a Receipt. Even then no second Receipt is written, because the Invocation owner's cancellation path re-reads its own state and reports the item settled before it asks the target.

Recorded discrimination is owed and is not this row's to write. artifacts/quality/discrimination/ is W0-owned and every cited file post-dates the last mutation run, so a verified status would add a DISC-STALE issue. Promotion needs a W0 run recording a kill inside TurnAdmissionVerifier.admit, TurnAdmissionIdentity.owner, Run.acknowledgeDelivery and RunRuntime's cancellation-message enumeration.

bounds: A model input's coverage claim is per-record while its omission fact is per-section, so a commit carried in fully-reduced form is indistinguishable in the record from one carried whole; the rule does not claim per-commit attribution of withheld bytes and no reconstruction depends on it. Correcting it means adding a per-commit omission to the record, which is an ADDITIVE optional field that forks no existing modelInputCommitId - measured: an absent optional key encodes identically - but the accompanying section 5.6 prose moves this atom's own specTextSha256, so it is a declared digest re-affirmation and not a silent edit. (W5, CompactionConcept.)

The shape choice above is load-bearing rather than stylistic, and stating which shape is safe is the point of recording it: the natural replacement, covers carrying {commit, omission} elements, does fork every modelInputCommitId, because TurnModelInput.toData() reaches a content-addressed ref that becomes the commit id - a derivation MIGRATE-OPERATION-DESCRIPTOR-PRESENCE already names. TurnShownContent.toData()'s inline XOR ref is the in-record precedent for emitting an optional key only when non-empty. On whether any deployment already holds run.commit records of kind modelInput under the old derivation: negative for the Cloudflare substrate only, established by absence of a write path rather than by inventory - no RunCommit occurrence in that adapter's source, no run-commit store among its durable tables, and its only references in-memory test fixtures. That closes the question for that substrate and says nothing about any other host.
